quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no visible damage. If a helmet has been in a crash, you should replace it.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can stop other vehicles from sharing their lane by:

options.text: Riding on the left side of the lane.
Riding in the center of the lane.
Giving dirty looks to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to make it harder for other vehicles to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily buildup. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center of the lane.
Not worry about oil or debris in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it rains.
questions.explanation: Oil builds up in the center of lanes from car and truck drippings. This strip usually has enough grip in dry conditions. It is narrow enough that you can ride around it while still staying in the center of your lane. Avoid it when the road is wet.

questions.question: If you brake while turning a curve:

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the turn.
You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When your motorcycle leans into a turn, some tire grip is used for turning. This means less grip is available for braking.

questions.question: In crashes between motorcycles and cars, how many are caused by drivers failing to yield the right-of-way to the rider?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars happen because the car driver did not yield the right-of-way to the rider.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This keeps them from falling behind the group and lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane so others see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: If the throttle gets stuck, you should:

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle sticks, try twisting it back and forth several times. If it stays stuck, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: Which part of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left side of the lane
The right side of the lane
No part of the lane should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No part of the lane should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best and no position should always be avoided. Choose a lane position that matches your riding conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Keep a greater distance from other vehicles.
Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always tell your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should ride in what formation?
questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when riding through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. This is safer than a staggered formation.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratched and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
They should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
They should not allow any air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratched and become brittle, so they need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Plastic face shields and goggles develop scratches and become brittle over time. Replace them regularly to keep your protection and comfort at their best.

questions.question: What should you do when riding in a group?

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back.
Don't ride too close to other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't ride too close to other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors regularly. Put experienced riders at the front and back. Keep enough space between you and other riders at all times.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and brake harder.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Don't brake and swerve at the same time. You need good traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each lane has three paths: left, center, and right. You can position your motorcycle in any of these areas.

questions.question: How should you load cargo onto a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Load items over or in front of the rear axle. Putting cargo behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a rider is how many times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: How can you increase the chance that other drivers will see you at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a lane position that is easy for oncoming traffic to see. Maintain a good space cushion so you can move if needed. Don't assume other drivers see you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before hitting it.
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before impact. Try to hit the object at a 90-degree angle. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle just before impact.
